title: Conjugate adjunction transfer of the projection tensor transpose
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be symmetric monoidal categories, with tensor, units $\mathbf1_{\mathcal C},\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}$, left unitors $\lambda$ and right unitors $r$ [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. A symmetry $\sigma_{B,C}:B\otimes C\xrightarrow{\sim}C\otimes B$ is natural, involutive, satisfies the hexagon identities, and obeys $\lambda_B\circ\sigma_{B,\mathbf1}=r_B$. Let $F,S:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $G,T:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ have adjunctions $F\dashv G$ and $S\dashv T$, counits $\varepsilon,\operatorname{ev}$ and natural Hom bijections $J_F,J_S$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Choose natural isomorphisms $d:F\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ and $u:T\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}$. For $M\in\mathcal C,K\in\mathcal D$, choose isomorphisms natural in both variables
$$P_{M,K}:FM\otimes K\xrightarrow{\sim}F(M\otimes TK),\qquad p_{M,K}:SM\otimes K\xrightarrow{\sim}S(M\otimes TK).$$
Assume, for all $M,K$,
$$d_{M\otimes TK}\circ P_{M,K}=p_{M,K}\circ(d_M\otimes1_K).$$
Put $a_K=\lambda_{TK}\circ(u\otimes1_{TK})$ and assume
$$\operatorname{ev}_K\circ S(a_K)\circ p_{T\mathbf1_{\mathcal D},K}=\lambda_K\circ(\operatorname{ev}_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}}\otimes1_K).$$
Define the conjugate $\rho=(d^{-1})^c:G\to T$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], $W=G\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}$, $\eta=u\circ\rho_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}}$, and
$$q_K=\lambda_K\circ(\varepsilon_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}}\otimes1_K)\circ P_{W,K}^{-1}\circ F(\sigma_{TK,W}),\qquad\tau_K=J_F(q_K).$$
Then $\rho$ is a natural isomorphism uniquely characterized by
$$\operatorname{ev}_K\circ S(\rho_K)\circ d_{GK}=\varepsilon_K.$$
For every $N\in\mathcal C$, $K\in\mathcal D$ and $b:FN\to K$,
$$J_S(b\circ d_N^{-1})=\rho_K\circ J_F(b).$$
Moreover, naturally in $K$, with $N=TK\otimes W$,
$$q_K\circ d_N^{-1}=\lambda_K\circ((\varepsilon_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}}\circ d_W^{-1})\otimes1_K)\circ p_{W,K}^{-1}\circ S(\sigma_{TK,W})=\operatorname{ev}_K\circ S(r_{TK}\circ(1_{TK}\otimes\eta)),$$
$$\rho_K\circ\tau_K=r_{TK}\circ(1_{TK}\otimes\eta).$$
These are equalities of morphisms and of the natural transformations in $K$ that they define; no faithfulness of $F,S,G,T$ and no monoidal structure on $F$ or $S$ is assumed.

proof.text:
The conjugation bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] applied to $d^{-1}:S\to F$ gives the natural isomorphism $\rho:G\to T$. In the identity-vertical-functor case, the transpose characterization in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] says exactly
$$\operatorname{ev}_K S(\rho_K)=\varepsilon_K d_{GK}^{-1}.$$
Right composition with $d_{GK}$ gives the asserted counit equation. Conversely that equation determines each $\rho_K$ by the injectivity of $J_S^{-1}:\operatorname{Hom}(GK,TK)\to\operatorname{Hom}(SGK,K)$, so it also determines the natural transformation uniquely.

proof.text: Expand both Hom transposes using the adjunction units. The Mathlib identity unit_conjugateEquiv identifies the unit followed by T(d.inv) with the F-adjunction unit followed by the conjugate. Naturality of the conjugate at b then gives J_S(d.inv followed by b) = J_F(b) followed by the conjugate. This is the identity-vertical case of the mate-transpose calculation, proved directly from [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] and the Hom-transpose definition [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate].

proof.text:
Put $N=TK\otimes W$ and $e=\varepsilon_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}}d_W^{-1}:SW\to\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}$. Naturality of $d$ at $\sigma_{TK,W}$ and the assumed projection square give, respectively,
$$F(\sigma_{TK,W})d_N^{-1}=d_{W\otimes TK}^{-1}S(\sigma_{TK,W}),\qquad P_{W,K}^{-1}d_{W\otimes TK}^{-1}=(d_W^{-1}\otimes1_K)p_{W,K}^{-1}.$$
Substitute both identities into the definition of $q_K$, and compose the two tensor morphisms using bifunctoriality [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. The result is exactly
$$q_Kd_N^{-1}=\lambda_K(e\otimes1_K)p_{W,K}^{-1}S(\sigma_{TK,W}).$$

source.place: Step 1, etale normalization of the tensor map; explicit categorical calculation by Q21, serving thm-pur-composition-coherence proof Step 1, remaining co-projection factors

proof.text:
Write $R=\rho_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}}:W\to T\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}$. Step 1 gives $e=\operatorname{ev}_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}}S(R)$. Naturality of $p$ in its first variable gives
$$(S(R)\otimes1_K)p_{W,K}^{-1}=p_{T\mathbf1_{\mathcal D},K}^{-1}S(R\otimes1_{TK}).$$
Multiply the assumed unit-evaluation equation on the right by $p_{T\mathbf1_{\mathcal D},K}^{-1}$ and substitute these identities into Step 3. Functoriality yields
$$q_Kd_N^{-1}=\operatorname{ev}_K S\bigl(a_K(R\otimes1_{TK})\sigma_{TK,W}\bigr).$$
Only the stated evaluation identity at $T\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}$ is used; no evaluation identity at arbitrary objects is needed.

proof.text:
Since $\eta=uR$, the morphism inside $S$ in Step 4 is
$$\lambda_{TK}(\eta\otimes1_{TK})\sigma_{TK,W}.$$
Naturality of the given symmetry at $(1_{TK},\eta)$ identifies $(\eta\otimes1_{TK})\sigma_{TK,W}$ with $\sigma_{TK,\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}}(1_{TK}\otimes\eta)$. The assumed identity $\lambda_{TK}\sigma_{TK,\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}}=r_{TK}$ therefore makes this morphism
$$h_K:=r_{TK}(1_{TK}\otimes\eta).$$
Thus $q_Kd_N^{-1}=\operatorname{ev}_K S(h_K)$, proving the second expression for the required composite. This is just substitution and symmetry naturality, not a monoidal structure on $S$.

source.place: Step 1, etale normalization of the tensor map; explicit categorical calculation by Q21, serving thm-pur-composition-coherence proof Step 1, remaining co-projection factors

proof.text:
The inverse $S\dashv T$ Hom bijection sends $h:N\to TK$ to $\operatorname{ev}_K S(h)$ (the counit-transpose convention of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]). Hence Step 5 gives $J_S(q_Kd_N^{-1})=h_K$. Apply Step 2 to $b=q_K$ and use $\tau_K=J_F(q_K)$ to obtain
$$\rho_K\tau_K=h_K=r_{TK}(1_{TK}\otimes\eta).$$
All equalities were obtained inside Hom sets by bijectivity or substitution, with no cancellation through $F$ or $S$.

source.place: Step 1, etale normalization of the tensor map; explicit categorical calculation by Q21, serving thm-pur-composition-coherence proof Step 1, remaining co-projection factors

proof.text:
For completeness the naturality assertions can be checked directly. For $f:K\to L$ in $\mathcal D$, naturality of symmetry, $P^{-1}$ and the left unitor gives the three successive equations
$$F(\sigma_{TL,W})F(Tf\otimes1_W)=F(1_W\otimes Tf)F(\sigma_{TK,W}),$$
$$P_{W,L}^{-1}F(1_W\otimes Tf)=(1_{FW}\otimes f)P_{W,K}^{-1},$$
$$\lambda_L(\varepsilon_{\mathbf1}\otimes1_L)(1_{FW}\otimes f)=f\lambda_K(\varepsilon_{\mathbf1}\otimes1_K).$$
Their composite is $q_LF(Tf\otimes1_W)=fq_K$. Naturality of the assumed Hom bijections then gives $\tau_L(Tf\otimes1_W)=G(f)\tau_K$. Likewise $h_L(Tf\otimes1_W)=Tf\,h_K$ by naturality of $r$ and bifunctoriality. Finally $d^{-1}$ is natural, so $q_Kd_N^{-1}$ is natural; its two equal expressions from Steps 3 and 5 inherit that same naturality. Thus the componentwise equalities are equalities of the stated natural transformations.
